subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a load-time repair that drops only dead-end `type: "compaction"` siblings from persisted session JSONL, or require a write-side retry/idempotency fix before persisted cleanup ships?
rationale: The remaining implementation choice can delete selected persisted session entries during repair, which is a session-state policy decision rather than a routine code-shape choice.

options.title: Refresh and land the narrow repair
options.body: Update the linked PR or a replacement branch to current main, keep the compaction-only drop rule, and add focused regression coverage for the reported fork shape and safe side branches.

options.title: Prioritize write-side prevention
options.body: Hold the load-time cleanup until compaction retry writes are made idempotent or superseded at the source, accepting that already-corrupted JSONL may remain unrepaired longer.

options.title: Diagnostics-only recovery
options.body: Reject deletion during repair and instead add detection/reporting guidance for manual recovery from pre-fork checkpoints.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land the narrow repair
recommendation.body: Update the linked PR or a replacement branch to current main, keep the compaction-only drop rule, and add focused regression coverage for the reported fork shape and safe side branches.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-runtime refactor and repair commits make steipete the best available routing candidate for the persistence-policy choice.
